content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository lowRISC_ibex_pr1872, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# insn_trigger_exception coverpoint does not work
The test riscv_debug_triggers_test added in #1801 generates stimulus to hit [this coverpoint](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/blob/ce536ae47677e952de02b7421e1b78efb5761ab2/dv/uvm/core_ibex/fcov/core_ibex_fcov_if.sv#L502), but it does not trigger.
```verilog
// > core_ibex_fcov_if.sv
// L502
DV_FCOV_EXPR_SEEN(insn_trigger_exception, instr_id_matches_trigger_q &&
id_stage_i.controller_i.fcov_pipe_flush)
```
REPRO
```
// Checkout https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/pull/1801
make TEST=riscv_debug_triggers_test ITERATIONS=1 SEED=14664 COV=1 -j12 -ik
// The instruction/event that should trigger this coverpoint can be seen retiring at t = 1010124 ns
```

279   // This latch is needed because if we cannot register this condition being true
280   // with a clock. Being in the sleep mode implies that we don't have an active clock.
281   // So, we need to catch the condition, latch it and keep it until we wake up and decode
282   // an instruction (which guarantees we have a clock in the core)
283   logic kept_wfi_with_irq;
284 
285   always_latch begin
286     if (id_stage_i.controller_i.ctrl_fsm_cs == DECODE) begin
287       kept_wfi_with_irq = 1'b0;
288     end else if (id_stage_i.controller_i.ctrl_fsm_cs == SLEEP &&
289                  id_stage_i.controller_i.ctrl_fsm_ns == SLEEP &&
290                  (|cs_registers_i.mip)) begin
291       kept_wfi_with_irq = 1'b1;
292     end
293   end

299 
300   // Delay instruction matching trigger point since it is catched in IF stage.
301   // We would want to cross it with decoded instruction categories and it does not matter
302   // when exactly we are hitting the condition.
303   always @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
304     if (!rst_ni) begin
305       instr_id_matches_trigger_q <= 1'b0;
306     end else begin

311   // Keep track of previous data addr of Store to catch RAW hazard caused by STORE->LOAD
312   logic [31:0]     prev_store_addr;
313   logic [31:0]     data_addr_incr;
314   logic [31:0]     curr_data_addr;
315   logic            raw_hz;

317   always @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
318     if (!rst_ni) begin
319       prev_store_addr <= 1'b0;
320     end else if (load_store_unit_i.data_we_o) begin
321       // It does not matter if the store we executed before load is misaligned or not. Because
322       // even if it is misaligned, we would catch the "corrected" version (2nd access) before
323       // doing the RAW hazard check.
324       prev_store_addr <= load_store_unit_i.data_addr_o;
325     end
326   end
327 
328   // Calculate the corrected version of the new data addr at the same time while LOAD instruction
329   // gets decoded.
330   always_comb begin
331     if (load_store_unit_i.split_misaligned_access) begin
332       data_addr_incr = load_store_unit_i.data_addr + 4;
333       curr_data_addr = {data_addr_incr[2+:30],2'b00};
334     end else begin
335       curr_data_addr = load_store_unit_i.data_addr;
336     end
337   end

339   // If we have LOAD at ID/EX stage and STORE at WB stage, compare the calculated address for LOAD
